segments.tr: - **Intensitas distribusi** — berapa banyak outlet yang membawa produk: intensif (di mana-mana), selektif (serangkaian yang dikurasi), atau eksklusif (satu per wilayah).

segments.src: - **Omnichannel** — channels integrated to share inventory, pricing, and customer data so the experience feels like one brand, versus multichannel silos.
segments.tr: - **Omnichannel** — saluran terintegrasi untuk berbagi persediaan, harga, dan data pelanggan sehingga pengalaman terasa seperti satu merek, versus silo multisaluran.

segments.src: - **Channel conflict** — friction that arises when a new or existing channel undercuts another, e.g., a brand's direct site competing with its own retail partners.
segments.tr: - **Konflik saluran** — gesekan yang timbul ketika saluran baru atau yang sudah ada mengalahkan yang lain, misalnya, situs langsung merek bersaing dengan mitra ritel mereka sendiri.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — C.** Maximum coverage for a low-consideration convenience good; shoppers won't search, so absence equals a lost sale.
segments.tr: *Jawaban: **Q1 — C.** Cakupan maksimum untuk barang kenyamanan pertimbangan rendah; pembeli tidak akan mencari, jadi ketidakhadiran sama dengan penjualan yang hilang.

segments.src: **Q2 — X (False).** That's multichannel.
segments.tr: **Q2 — S (Salah).** Itu multisaluran.

segments.src: It only becomes omnichannel when the channels share inventory, pricing, and customer history — app stock visibility, in-store returns for online orders, and so on.
segments.tr: Ini hanya menjadi omnichannel ketika saluran berbagi persediaan, harga, dan riwayat pelanggan — visibilitas stok aplikasi, pengembalian di toko untuk pesanan online, dan seterusnya.

segments.src: **Q3 — B.** Channel functions can be shifted, not eliminated; whoever drops out hands the warehousing, shipping, credit, and returns work to someone else — usually the brand.
segments.tr: **Q3 — B.** Fungsi saluran dapat digeser, bukan dihilangkan; siapa pun yang keluar menyerahkan pekerjaan pergudangan, pengiriman, kredit, dan pengembalian kepada orang lain — biasanya merek.

segments.src: Prices don't automatically drop (A and C are the classic misconception), and going direct typically *increases* conflict risk rather than removing it (D).*
segments.tr: Harga tidak turun secara otomatis (A dan C adalah salah paham klasik), dan langsung biasanya *meningkatkan* risiko konflik daripada menghapusnya (D).*

ja.title: [Marketing 101 #9] 最高の製品は勝ちません。実際に手に入れられるものが勝つのです。

segments.src: > "Place" isn't about where a product sits. It's about how many steps stand between wanting it and holding it — and who does the work of removing them.
segments.tr: > "Place" は製品がどこに置いてあるかについてではありません。それは、製品が欲しいと思ってから手に入れるまでに何段階のステップがあるか、そしてそれらを取り除く作業を誰が行うかについてです。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 本日のコンセプト

segments.src: Of marketing's four Ps — product, price, promotion, place — **place** is the least glamorous and quietly the most decisive.
segments.tr: マーケティングの4つのP — 製品、価格、プロモーション、流通 — の中で、**流通**は最も地味でありながら、静かに最も決定的です。

segments.src: It's shorthand for *distribution*: the path a product travels from whoever made it to whoever uses it.
segments.tr: これは*流通*の略語です：製品を製造した者から、それを使う者までの経路です。

segments.src: Two questions define that path.
segments.tr: その経路を定義する2つの質問があります。

segments.src: How many hops?**
segments.tr: 何段階ですか？**

segments.src: A **direct channel** goes maker → customer: a farmers market stand, a brand's own website, a factory outlet.
segments.tr: **直接チャネル**は製造者→顧客：ファーマーズマーケットの店舗、ブランド自身のウェブサイト、工場直売店です。

segments.src: An **indirect channel** adds **intermediaries**: manufacturer → wholesaler/distributor → retailer → you.
segments.tr: **間接チャネル**は**中間業者**を加えます：メーカー→卸売業者/流通業者→小売業者→あなた。

segments.src: Each hop takes a slice of margin.
segments.tr: 各段階は利益の一部を取ります。

segments.src: Each hop also does real work.
segments.tr: 各段階は実際の仕事も行います。

segments.src: That's the part people get wrong.
segments.tr: それが人々が間違える部分です。

segments.src: The common complaint is that middlemen are markup for nothing.
segments.tr: 一般的な不満は、中間業者は何の価値もない上乗せだということです。

segments.src: But distribution functions can be *shifted*, not *eliminated*.
segments.tr: しかし、流通機能は*排除*されるのではなく、*転嫁*することができます。

segments.src: Somebody has to:
segments.tr: 誰かが以下をしなければなりません：

segments.src: - **Break bulk** — turn a truckload into a shelf's worth
segments.tr: - **バルク分割** — トラック1台分を棚単位に分割する

segments.src: - **Carry inventory** and absorb the risk that it doesn't sell
segments.tr: - **在庫を保有し**、売れないリスクを吸収する

segments.src: - **Extend credit** so a small store can stock before it sells
segments.tr: - **後払いを提供する** — 小売店が売る前に仕入れができるようにする

segments.src: - **Assemble assortment** so you don't visit 40 brand websites for one shopping trip
segments.tr: - **品揃え** — 1回の買い物で40ブランドのウェブサイトを訪問する必要がないようにする

segments.src: - **Handle returns**, damage, and customer questions
segments.tr: - **返品を処理する**、損傷対応、顧客対応

segments.src: Cut the distributor and you inherit the warehouse, the trucks, the credit risk, and the returns desk.
segments.tr: 流通業者を削除すると、倉庫、トラック、信用リスク、返品デスクを引き継ぎます。

segments.src: Sometimes that's worth it.
segments.tr: 時にはそれは価値があります。

segments.src: It's never free.
segments.tr: それは決して無料ではありません。

segments.src: How widely?**
segments.tr: どのくらい広く？**

segments.src: This is **distribution intensity**, and it has three settings:
segments.tr: これは**流通密度**であり、3つの設定があります：

segments.src: - **Intensive** — everywhere physically possible. Soda, gum, phone chargers, sunscreen. Nobody drives across town for a Coke; if it isn't there, the sale goes to whatever *is*.
segments.tr: - **集約的** — 物理的に可能な限り至る所。ソーダ、ガム、携帯充電器、日焼け止め。誰もコークのために町を横切ってドライブしません。そこになければ、売上は別の場所に流れます。

segments.src: - **Selective** — a curated set of partners. Appliances, mid-tier cosmetics, running shoes. Enough coverage to be findable, few enough to keep service quality up.
segments.tr: - **選別的** — キュレーションされたパートナーのセット。電化製品、ミッドティアのコスメティクス、ランニングシューズ。見つけられるのに十分なカバレッジで、サービス品質を維持するのに十分な数。

segments.src: - **Exclusive** — one partner per territory. Luxury watches, car dealerships, high-end audio. Scarcity and service are part of the product.
segments.tr: - **排他的** — 地域ごとに1つのパートナー。高級時計、自動車ディーラー、高級オーディオ。希少性とサービスは製品の一部です。

segments.src: The right setting follows how people shop.
segments.tr: 正しい流通密度は、消費者がどのように買い物をするかに従います。

segments.src: The less someone is willing to search, the more intensive you must be.
segments.tr: 消費者の検索意欲が低いほど、より集約的な流通が必要になります。

segments.src: **Multichannel vs.
segments.tr: **マルチチャネル対

segments.src: omnichannel.** These get used interchangeably and shouldn't be.
segments.tr: オムニチャネル。** これらは相互に交換可能に使用されていますが、そうすべきではありません。

segments.src: *Multichannel* means you sell in several places, each running as its own silo — the website has no idea what the store has.
segments.tr: *マルチチャネル*は、複数の場所で販売することを意味し、それぞれが独自のサイロとして実行されます — ウェブサイトは店舗が何を持っているかを知りません。

segments.src: *Omnichannel* means those channels share inventory, pricing, and customer history, so the shopper experiences one brand instead of three departments.
segments.tr: *オムニチャネル*は、これらのチャネルが在庫、価格、顧客履歴を共有することを意味し、買い物客は3つの部門ではなく1つのブランドを経験します。

segments.src: Buy online / pick up in store, return an online order at the register, ship-from-store, an app that shows real stock at the location nearest you — those are omnichannel plumbing, not marketing copy.
segments.tr: オンラインで購入して店舗でピックアップする、レジでオンライン注文を返品する、店舗から配送する、最も近い場所での実在庫を表示するアプリ — これらはオムニチャネルの仕組み、マーケティングコピーではありません。

segments.src: **Channel conflict** is the standard failure mode: a new channel eats an existing one.
segments.tr: **チャネル競争**は標準的な失敗モードです：新しいチャネルが既存のものを蚕食します。

segments.src: A brand launches a direct site priced below the retailers who built its shelf presence, and those retailers quietly cut their orders.
segments.tr: ブランドがその棚の存在を構築した小売業者以下の価格で直接サイトを立ち上げると、それらの小売業者はひっそりと注文を削減します。

segments.src: Companies manage this with consistent pricing, channel-specific assortments (the exclusive colorway only Dick's gets), and minimum advertised price policies.
segments.tr: 企業はこれを一貫した価格設定、チャネル固有の品揃え（排他的なカラーウェイはDick'sだけが取得）、および最小広告価格ポリシーで管理します。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活の中で

segments.src: It's Thursday night in Dallas.
segments.tr: ダラスの木曜夜です。

segments.src: Your kid's birthday party is Saturday and the one thing they asked for is a specific LEGO set.
segments.tr: お子さんの誕生日パーティーは土曜日で、彼が欲しいのは特定のLEGOセットです。

segments.src: You have options, and each is a different channel structure.
segments.tr: 選択肢があり、それぞれが異なるチャネル構造です。

segments.src: LEGO's own site is **direct**.
segments.tr: LEGOの独自サイトは**直接**です。

segments.src: Amazon is a retailer plus a marketplace of third-party sellers.
segments.tr: Amazonは小売業者とサードパーティの売り手のマーケットプレイスです。

segments.src: Target and Walmart are **retailers** buying at wholesale.
segments.tr: TargetとWalmartは卸売で購入する**小売業者**です。

segments.src: The independent toy shop two miles away buys through a **distributor**.
segments.tr: 2マイル離れた独立した玩具屋は**流通業者**を通じて購入します。

segments.src: You open the Target app, see that the store off I-35 has one on the shelf, order it, and pick it up in an hour.
segments.tr: あなたはTargetアプリを開き、I-35脇の店舗の棚に商品があることを確認して、注文して1時間で受け取ります。

segments.src: Trace what had to happen for that hour to exist.
segments.tr: その1時間が成立するために何が起こらなければならなかったかを追跡してみます。

segments.src: The set was molded in a factory, containerized, shipped across an ocean, cleared customs, sat in a regional distribution center, rode a truck to that store, got scanned onto a shelf — and the app knew, at store level, that it was there.
segments.tr: セットは工場で成形され、コンテナ化され、海を越えて出荷され、税関を通過し、地域流通センターに置かれ、トラックでその店舗に運ばれ、棚にスキャンされました — そしてアプリは店舗レベルで、それがそこにあることを知っていました。

segments.src: That last part is the omnichannel piece.
segments.tr: その最後の部分がオムニチャネルの部分です。

segments.src: Same price in the aisle and in the app; an employee picks it; and if it's the wrong set, you can return it at the counter even though you "bought it online."
segments.tr: 通路とアプリで同じ価格。従業員がピックアップします。そして、それが間違ったセットの場合、たとえ「オンラインで購入した」としても、カウンターでそれを返すことができます。

segments.src: The little toy shop has it too, at full price.
segments.tr: 小さな玩具屋も完全な価格でそれを持っています。

segments.src: It can stock a few thousand different items without opening a few thousand supplier accounts, because a distributor bought the pallet and sold it a case of six.
segments.tr: 流通業者がパレットを購入して6ケースで販売したため、数千のサプライヤーアカウントを開くことなく、数千の異なるアイテムを在庫できます。

segments.src: That's breaking bulk, and it's the entire reason small retail can exist.
segments.tr: これがバルク分割であり、小売業が存在する全体的な理由です。

segments.src: Now the brand's side of the tradeoff, using illustrative numbers (not LEGO's real ones):
segments.tr: ここで、説明的な数字（LEGOの実際の数字ではなく）を使用したブランド側のトレードオフを見てみます：

segments.src: Direct (brand.com)
segments.tr: Direct (brand.com)

segments.src: $49.99 paid  -  ~$7 pick/pack/ship  -  ~$4 payments & returns   =  ~$39 to the brand
segments.tr: $49.99 paid  -  ~$7 pick/pack/ship  -  ~$4 payments & returns   =  ~$39 to the brand

segments.src: Through retail
segments.tr: Through retail

segments.src: brand -> distributor: ~$22
segments.tr: brand -> distributor: ~$22

segments.src: distributor -> store: ~$28
segments.tr: distributor -> store: ~$28

segments.src: store -> shopper:     $49.99                                     =  ~$22 to the brand
segments.tr: store -> shopper:     $49.99                                     =  ~$22 to the brand

segments.src: Direct looks like a landslide — until you ask how many people were going to type your URL on a Thursday night.
segments.tr: 直接販売は圧倒的に見えます — 木曜夜にあなたのURLを入力しに来る顧客が何人いるかを尋ねるまでは。

segments.src: Retail costs more than half the margin and delivers something direct can't manufacture: being already there, in the store the customer was going to anyway.
segments.tr: 小売は利益の半分以上の費用がかかり、直接販売ができないものを提供します：すでにそこにいること、顧客がとにかく行こうとしていた店舗で。

segments.src: Most brands run both, and spend a lot of effort keeping them from cannibalizing each other.
segments.tr: ほとんどのブランドは両方を実行し、それらが互いに蚕食するのを防ぐために多くの努力を費やします。

segments.src: That's the whole discipline in one sentence: **place is the practice of buying availability, and deciding what it's worth.**
segments.tr: それが全体の分野を1文で述べたものです：**流通は可用性を購入し、それが何の価値があるかを決定する実践です。**

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3行の要約

segments.src: 1. Place = distribution: the route from maker to user, defined by how many intermediaries are in it and how widely the product is stocked.
segments.tr: 1. Place = 流通：メーカーからユーザーへのルート。中間業者の数と製品が在庫される広さで定義される。

segments.src: 2. Intermediaries aren't optional overhead — they perform functions (breaking bulk, inventory risk, credit, assortment, returns) that someone has to perform, so removing them means absorbing them.
segments.tr: 2. 中間業者はオプションの間接費ではありません — 誰かが果たさなければならない機能（バルク分割、在庫リスク、信用供与、品揃え、返品処理）を実行するため、彼らを削除することは、これらの機能を自分で引き受けることを意味します。

segments.src: 3. Omnichannel isn't "selling in many places"; it's channels sharing inventory, price, and customer data so the shopper meets one brand — and adding channels always risks conflict with the ones you already have.
segments.tr: 3. オムニチャネルは「多くの場所での販売」ではありません。チャネルが在庫、価格、顧客データを共有し、買い物客が一つのブランドに会い、チャネルの追加は常にすでに持っているものとの競争のリスクをもたらします。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自己診断テスト

segments.src: **Q1.** A beverage company wants its new sports drink in every gas station, vending machine, and grocery store it can reach.
segments.tr: **Q1.** 飲料会社が新しいスポーツドリンクをあらゆるガソリンスタンド、自動販売機、食料品店に置きたいと考えています。

segments.src: Which distribution intensity is this?
segments.tr: これはどの流通密度ですか？

segments.src: A) Exclusive B) Selective C) Intensive D) Direct-only
segments.tr: A) 排他的 B) 選別的 C) 集約的 D) 直接のみ

segments.src: **Q2.** (O/X) A company that sells through its website, a mobile app, and physical stores is by definition running an omnichannel strategy.
segments.tr: **Q2.** (○/×) ウェブサイト、モバイルアプリ、実店舗を通じて販売する企業は、定義上、オムニチャネル戦略を実行しています。

segments.src: **Q3.** A furniture brand shuts down its wholesale distributor to "cut out the middleman."
segments.tr: **Q3.** 家具ブランドが「中間業者を排除する」ために卸売流通業者をシャットダウンします。

segments.src: Which is the most likely consequence?
segments.tr: 最も可能性の高い結果は何ですか？

segments.src: A) The distribution functions disappear along with the distributor
segments.tr: A) 流通機能は流通業者とともに消えます

segments.src: B) The brand must now carry inventory, ship to stores, and manage returns itself
segments.tr: B) ブランドは現在、在庫を保有し、店舗に出荷し、返品を自分で管理しなければなりません

segments.src: C) Retail prices automatically fall by the distributor's full margin
segments.tr: C) 小売価格は流通業者の完全な利益で自動的に下がります

segments.src: D) Channel conflict becomes impossible
segments.tr: D) チャネル競争は不可能になります

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 本日の用語

segments.src: - **Distribution channel** — the set of organizations that move a product from producer to end user.
segments.tr: - **流通チャネル** — 製品をプロデューサーから最終ユーザーに移動させる組織のセット。

segments.src: - **Intermediary** — a wholesaler, distributor, or retailer that performs channel functions such as breaking bulk, holding inventory, and extending credit.
segments.tr: - **中間業者** — バルク分割、在庫保有、信用供与などのチャネル機能を実行する卸売業者、流通業者、または小売業者。

segments.src: - **Distribution intensity** — how many outlets carry the product: intensive (everywhere), selective (a curated set), or exclusive (one per territory).
segments.tr: - **流通密度** — どのくらい多くのアウトレットが製品を運ぶか：集約的（至る所）、選別的（キュレーションされたセット）、または排他的（地域ごとに1つ）。

segments.src: - **Omnichannel** — channels integrated to share inventory, pricing, and customer data so the experience feels like one brand, versus multichannel silos.
segments.tr: - **オムニチャネル** — マルチチャネルのサイロとは異なり、在庫、価格設定、および顧客データを共有するために統合されたチャネルで、1つのブランドのように感じられます。

segments.src: - **Channel conflict** — friction that arises when a new or existing channel undercuts another, e.g., a brand's direct site competing with its own retail partners.
segments.tr: - **チャネル競争** — 新しいまたは既存のチャネルが別のチャネルを台無しにするときに生じる摩擦。例えば、ブランドの直接サイトが独自の小売パートナーと競合します。

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — C.** Maximum coverage for a low-consideration convenience good; shoppers won't search, so absence equals a lost sale.
segments.tr: *答え：**Q1 — C.** 低関心の便利商品の最大カバレッジ。買い物客は検索しないため、不在は失われた売上と等しい。

segments.src: **Q2 — X (False).** That's multichannel.
segments.tr: **Q2 — × (偽)。** それはマルチチャネルです。

segments.src: It only becomes omnichannel when the channels share inventory, pricing, and customer history — app stock visibility, in-store returns for online orders, and so on.
segments.tr: チャネルが在庫、価格設定、顧客履歴を共有するときにのみオムニチャネルになります — アプリの在庫可視性、オンライン注文の店舗返品など。

segments.src: **Q3 — B.** Channel functions can be shifted, not eliminated; whoever drops out hands the warehousing, shipping, credit, and returns work to someone else — usually the brand.
segments.tr: **Q3 — B.** チャネル機能は排除されるのではなくシフト（転嫁）できます。脱落した者は倉庫保管、配送、信用供与、返品処理を他の誰か（通常はブランド）に引き渡します。

segments.src: Prices don't automatically drop (A and C are the classic misconception), and going direct typically *increases* conflict risk rather than removing it (D).*
segments.tr: 価格は自動的に下がりません（AとCは古典的な誤解です）、そして直接販売に行くことは、それを削除するのではなく、競争リスクを通常*増加させます*（D）。*

de.title: [Marketing 101 #9] Das beste Produkt gewinnt nicht. Dasjenige, das man tatsächlich bekommen kann, tut es.

segments.src: > "Place" isn't about where a product sits. It's about how many steps stand between wanting it and holding it — and who does the work of removing them.
segments.tr: > "Place" ist nicht darum, wo ein Produkt sitzt. Es geht darum, wie viele Schritte zwischen dem Wunsch danach und dem Besitz stehen – und wer die Arbeit leistet, sie zu entfernen.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Das heutige Konzept

segments.src: Of marketing's four Ps — product, price, promotion, place — **place** is the least glamorous and quietly the most decisive.
segments.tr: Von Marketings vier Ps — Produkt, Preis, Promotion, Place – ist **Place** das am wenigsten glamourös und leise das entscheidendste.

segments.src: It's shorthand for *distribution*: the path a product travels from whoever made it to whoever uses it.
segments.tr: Es ist Kurzform für *Vertrieb*: der Weg, den ein Produkt vom Hersteller zum Benutzer nimmt.

segments.src: Two questions define that path.
segments.tr: Zwei Fragen definieren diesen Weg.

segments.src: How many hops?**
segments.tr: Wie viele Zwischenschritte?**

segments.src: A **direct channel** goes maker → customer: a farmers market stand, a brand's own website, a factory outlet.
segments.tr: Ein **direkter Kanal** verläuft Hersteller → Kunde: ein Marktstand, die eigene Website einer Marke, ein Werksverkauf.

segments.src: An **indirect channel** adds **intermediaries**: manufacturer → wholesaler/distributor → retailer → you.
segments.tr: Ein **indirekter Kanal** fügt **Vermittler** hinzu: Hersteller → Großhändler/Distributor → Einzelhandel → Sie.

segments.src: Each hop takes a slice of margin.
segments.tr: Jeder Zwischenschritt kostet einen Teil der Gewinnmarge.

segments.src: Each hop also does real work.
segments.tr: Jeder Zwischenschritt leistet aber auch echte Arbeit.

segments.src: That's the part people get wrong.
segments.tr: Das ist der Teil, den Leute falsch verstehen.

segments.src: The common complaint is that middlemen are markup for nothing.
segments.tr: Das häufige Argument ist, dass Zwischenhändler nur unnötige Aufschläge sind.

segments.src: But distribution functions can be *shifted*, not *eliminated*.
segments.tr: Aber Vertriebsfunktionen können *verschoben*, nicht *beseitigt* werden.

segments.src: Somebody has to:
segments.tr: Jemand muss:

segments.src: - **Break bulk** — turn a truckload into a shelf's worth
segments.tr: - **Massenware aufteilen** — einen Lastwagen in Regalware umwandeln

segments.src: - **Carry inventory** and absorb the risk that it doesn't sell
segments.tr: - **Bestände halten** und das Risiko tragen, dass sich das Lager nicht verkauft

segments.src: - **Extend credit** so a small store can stock before it sells
segments.tr: - **Kredit gewähren**, damit ein kleines Geschäft vor dem Verkauf lagern kann

segments.src: - **Assemble assortment** so you don't visit 40 brand websites for one shopping trip
segments.tr: - **Sortiment zusammenstellen**, damit Sie nicht 40 Brand-Websites für einen Einkauf besuchen

segments.src: - **Handle returns**, damage, and customer questions
segments.tr: - **Rückgaben, Schäden und Kundenanfragen handhaben**

segments.src: Cut the distributor and you inherit the warehouse, the trucks, the credit risk, and the returns desk.
segments.tr: Streichen Sie den Distributor und Sie erben das Lagerhaus, die Lastwagen, das Kreditrisiko und die Rückgabeverwaltung.

segments.src: Sometimes that's worth it.
segments.tr: Manchmal lohnt sich das.

segments.src: It's never free.
segments.tr: Aber es ist niemals kostenlos.

segments.src: How widely?**
segments.tr: Wie weit verbreitet?**

segments.src: This is **distribution intensity**, and it has three settings:
segments.tr: Dies ist **Vertriebsintensität**, und sie hat drei Einstellungen:

segments.src: - **Intensive** — everywhere physically possible. Soda, gum, phone chargers, sunscreen. Nobody drives across town for a Coke; if it isn't there, the sale goes to whatever *is*.
segments.tr: - **Intensiv** — überall, wo es möglich ist. Limonade, Kaugummi, Telefonladegeräte, Sonnencreme. Niemand fährt über die halbe Stadt für eine Cola; wenn sie nicht da ist, geht der Verkauf zum nächsten verfügbaren Konkurrenzprodukt.

segments.src: - **Selective** — a curated set of partners. Appliances, mid-tier cosmetics, running shoes. Enough coverage to be findable, few enough to keep service quality up.
segments.tr: - **Selektiv** — ein kuratierter Satz von Partnern. Haushaltsgeräte, mittlere Kosmetika, Laufschuhe. Genug Präsenz um auffindbar zu sein, aber begrenzt genug um die Servicequalität zu sichern.

segments.src: - **Exclusive** — one partner per territory. Luxury watches, car dealerships, high-end audio. Scarcity and service are part of the product.
segments.tr: - **Exklusiv** — ein Partner pro Region. Luxusuhren, Autohändler, High-End-Audio. Exklusivität und Service sind Teil des Produkts.

segments.src: The right setting follows how people shop.
segments.tr: Die richtige Strategie folgt dem Einkaufsverhalten der Menschen.

segments.src: The less someone is willing to search, the more intensive you must be.
segments.tr: Je weniger jemand bereit ist zu suchen, desto intensiver muss die Verteilung sein.

segments.src: **Multichannel vs.
segments.tr: **Multichannel vs.

segments.src: omnichannel.** These get used interchangeably and shouldn't be.
segments.tr: Omnichannel.** Diese Begriffe werden oft verwechselt, sollten es aber nicht.

segments.src: *Multichannel* means you sell in several places, each running as its own silo — the website has no idea what the store has.
segments.tr: *Multichannel* bedeutet, dass Sie an mehreren Orten verkaufen, jeder läuft als separates Silo — die Website weiß nicht, was der Laden vorrätig hat.

segments.src: *Omnichannel* means those channels share inventory, pricing, and customer history, so the shopper experiences one brand instead of three departments.
segments.tr: *Omnichannel* bedeutet, dass diese Kanäle Bestand, Preise und Kundenhistorie teilen, sodass der Käufer eine einzige Marke statt mehrerer getrennte Abteilungen erlebt.

segments.src: Buy online / pick up in store, return an online order at the register, ship-from-store, an app that shows real stock at the location nearest you — those are omnichannel plumbing, not marketing copy.
segments.tr: Online kaufen/im Laden abholen, Online-Bestellung an der Kasse zurückgeben, vom Lager versenden, eine App zeigt verfügbaren Bestand am nächstgelegenen Ort — das sind Omnichannel-Infrastruktur, nicht nur Marketingtext.

segments.src: **Channel conflict** is the standard failure mode: a new channel eats an existing one.
segments.tr: **Kanalkonflikt** ist der Standard-Fehler: ein neuer Kanal verdrängt einen bestehenden.

segments.src: A brand launches a direct site priced below the retailers who built its shelf presence, and those retailers quietly cut their orders.
segments.tr: Eine Marke startet einen direkten Online-Shop mit niedrigeren Preisen als die Einzelhändler, die ihre Regalpräsenz aufgebaut haben, und diese Einzelhändler fahren ihre Bestellungen stillschweigend zurück.

segments.src: Companies manage this with consistent pricing, channel-specific assortments (the exclusive colorway only Dick's gets), and minimum advertised price policies.
segments.tr: Unternehmen handhaben dies durch einheitliche Preise, kanalspezifische Sortimente (die exklusive Farbe bekommen nur bestimmte Partner), und Mindestpreisrichtlinien.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: It's Thursday night in Dallas.
segments.tr: Es ist Donnerstagabend in Dallas.

segments.src: Your kid's birthday party is Saturday and the one thing they asked for is a specific LEGO set.
segments.tr: Die Geburtstagsparty Ihres Kindes ist am Samstag und das Einzige, das es sich wünscht, ist ein bestimmtes LEGO Set.

segments.src: You have options, and each is a different channel structure.
segments.tr: Sie haben mehrere Optionen, und jede ist eine andere Kanalstruktur.

segments.src: LEGO's own site is **direct**.
segments.tr: LEGOs eigene Website ist **direkt**.

segments.src: Amazon is a retailer plus a marketplace of third-party sellers.
segments.tr: Amazon ist ein Einzelhändler plus ein Marktplatz von Drittanbietern.

segments.src: Target and Walmart are **retailers** buying at wholesale.
segments.tr: Target und Walmart sind **Einzelhändler**, die im Großhandel einkaufen.

segments.src: The independent toy shop two miles away buys through a **distributor**.
segments.tr: Das unabhängige Spielzeuggeschäft zwei Meilen entfernt kauft über einen **Distributor**.

segments.src: You open the Target app, see that the store off I-35 has one on the shelf, order it, and pick it up in an hour.
segments.tr: Sie öffnen die Target-App, sehen, dass der Laden neben der I-35 ein Set im Regal hat, bestellen es und holen es in einer Stunde ab.

segments.src: Trace what had to happen for that hour to exist.
segments.tr: Nachdenken Sie darüber, was alles passieren musste, damit diese Stunde möglich wurde.

segments.src: The set was molded in a factory, containerized, shipped across an ocean, cleared customs, sat in a regional distribution center, rode a truck to that store, got scanned onto a shelf — and the app knew, at store level, that it was there.
segments.tr: Das Set wurde in einer Fabrik geprägt, in Container gepackt, über einen Ozean verschifft, durch den Zoll geleitet, in einem regionalen Vertriebszentrum gelagert, mit einem Laster zu dem Laden gefahren, ins Regalsystem eingescannt — und die App wusste auf Ladenebene, dass es dort war.

segments.src: That last part is the omnichannel piece.
segments.tr: Dieser letzte Teil ist die Omnichannel-Komponente.

segments.src: Same price in the aisle and in the app; an employee picks it; and if it's the wrong set, you can return it at the counter even though you "bought it online."
segments.tr: Gleicher Preis im Gang und in der App; ein Mitarbeiter pickt es; und wenn es das falsche Set ist, können Sie es an der Kasse zurückgeben, obwohl Sie "es online gekauft haben".

segments.src: The little toy shop has it too, at full price.
segments.tr: Das kleine Spielzeuggeschäft hat es auch, zum vollen Preis.

segments.src: It can stock a few thousand different items without opening a few thousand supplier accounts, because a distributor bought the pallet and sold it a case of six.
segments.tr: Es kann Tausende verschiedener Artikel lagern, ohne Tausende von Lieferantenkonten zu eröffnen, weil ein Distributor die Palette kaufte und es als Karton mit sechs Stück verkaufte.

segments.src: That's breaking bulk, and it's the entire reason small retail can exist.
segments.tr: Das ist Massenaufteilung, und das ist der Grund, warum kleiner Einzelhandel überhaupt existieren kann.

segments.src: Now the brand's side of the tradeoff, using illustrative numbers (not LEGO's real ones):
segments.tr: Betrachten wir nun die Seite der Marke, mit illustrativen Zahlen (nicht LEGOs echten):

segments.src: Direct (brand.com)
segments.tr: Direct (brand.com)

segments.src: $49.99 paid  -  ~$7 pick/pack/ship  -  ~$4 payments & returns   =  ~$39 to the brand
segments.tr: $49.99 paid  -  ~$7 pick/pack/ship  -  ~$4 payments & returns   =  ~$39 to the brand

segments.src: Through retail
segments.tr: Through retail

segments.src: brand -> distributor: ~$22
segments.tr: brand -> distributor: ~$22

segments.src: distributor -> store: ~$28
segments.tr: distributor -> store: ~$28

segments.src: store -> shopper:     $49.99                                     =  ~$22 to the brand
segments.tr: store -> shopper:     $49.99                                     =  ~$22 to the brand

segments.src: Direct looks like a landslide — until you ask how many people were going to type your URL on a Thursday night.
segments.tr: Direktverkauf sieht wie ein klarer Sieg aus — bis man fragt, wie viele Leute Ihre URL an einem Donnerstagabend eintippen würden.

segments.src: Retail costs more than half the margin and delivers something direct can't manufacture: being already there, in the store the customer was going to anyway.
segments.tr: Einzelhandel kostet mehr als die Hälfte der Gewinnmarge und bietet etwas, das Direktverkauf nicht kann: bereits da sein, im Laden, den der Kunde sowieso besucht.

segments.src: Most brands run both, and spend a lot of effort keeping them from cannibalizing each other.
segments.tr: Die meisten Marken nutzen beide Wege und investieren viel Aufwand um zu verhindern, dass sie sich gegenseitig kannibalisieren.

segments.src: That's the whole discipline in one sentence: **place is the practice of buying availability, and deciding what it's worth.**
segments.tr: Das ist die ganze Strategie in einem Satz: **Place ist die Kunst, Verfügbarkeit zu kaufen und zu entscheiden, was sie wert ist.**

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Zusammenfassung in 3 Zeilen

segments.src: 1. Place = distribution: the route from maker to user, defined by how many intermediaries are in it and how widely the product is stocked.
segments.tr: 1. Place = Vertrieb: der Weg vom Hersteller zum Nutzer, definiert durch die Anzahl der Zwischenhändler und wie flächendeckend das Produkt verfügbar ist.

segments.src: 2. Intermediaries aren't optional overhead — they perform functions (breaking bulk, inventory risk, credit, assortment, returns) that someone has to perform, so removing them means absorbing them.
segments.tr: 2. Zwischenhändler sind nicht optional — sie erfüllen Funktionen (Massenaufteilung, Lagerverwaltung, Kreditvergabe, Sortimentsaufbau, Rückgabenbearbeitung), die jemand ausführen muss; wer sie ausschaltet, übernimmt diese Aufgaben selbst.

segments.src: 3. Omnichannel isn't "selling in many places"; it's channels sharing inventory, price, and customer data so the shopper meets one brand — and adding channels always risks conflict with the ones you already have.
segments.tr: 3. Omnichannel ist nicht "an vielen Orten verkaufen"; es bedeutet, dass Kanäle Bestand, Preise und Kundendaten teilen, sodass der Käufer eine Marke erlebt — und neue Kanäle zu addieren birgt immer das Risiko von Konflikten mit bestehenden.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Selbsttest

segments.src: **Q1.** A beverage company wants its new sports drink in every gas station, vending machine, and grocery store it can reach.
segments.tr: **Frage 1.** Ein Getränkehersteller möchte sein neues Sportgetränk in jeder Tankstelle, jedem Automaten und jedem Supermarkt verfügbar machen, die er erreichen kann.

segments.src: Which distribution intensity is this?
segments.tr: Welche Vertriebsintensität ist das?

segments.src: A) Exclusive B) Selective C) Intensive D) Direct-only
segments.tr: A) Exklusiv B) Selektiv C) Intensiv D) Nur direkt

segments.src: **Q2.** (O/X) A company that sells through its website, a mobile app, and physical stores is by definition running an omnichannel strategy.
segments.tr: **Frage 2.** (R/F) Ein Unternehmen, das über seine Website, eine Mobile App und physische Läden verkauft, führt per Definition eine Omnichannel-Strategie durch.

segments.src: **Q3.** A furniture brand shuts down its wholesale distributor to "cut out the middleman."
segments.tr: **Frage 3.** Eine Möbelmarke beendet ihre Großhandelsdistribution um "den Zwischenhändler auszuschalten."

segments.src: Which is the most likely consequence?
segments.tr: Was ist die wahrscheinlichste Folge?

segments.src: A) The distribution functions disappear along with the distributor
segments.tr: A) Die Vertriebsfunktionen verschwinden mit dem Distributor

segments.src: B) The brand must now carry inventory, ship to stores, and manage returns itself
segments.tr: B) Die Marke muss jetzt selbst Bestände halten, zu Läden versenden und Rückgaben verwalten

segments.src: C) Retail prices automatically fall by the distributor's full margin
segments.tr: C) Die Einzelhandelspreise sinken automatisch um die volle Gewinnmarge des Distributors

segments.src: D) Channel conflict becomes impossible
segments.tr: D) Kanalkonflikt wird unmöglich

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Begriffe von heute

segments.src: - **Distribution channel** — the set of organizations that move a product from producer to end user.
segments.tr: - **Vertriebskanal** — die Organisationen, die ein Produkt vom Hersteller zum Endnutzer bringen.

segments.src: - **Intermediary** — a wholesaler, distributor, or retailer that performs channel functions such as breaking bulk, holding inventory, and extending credit.
segments.tr: - **Intermediär** — ein Großhändler, Distributor oder Einzelhändler, der Kanalfunktionen wie Massenaufteilung, Lagerhaltung und Kreditvergabe erfüllt.

segments.src: - **Distribution intensity** — how many outlets carry the product: intensive (everywhere), selective (a curated set), or exclusive (one per territory).
segments.tr: - **Vertriebsintensität** — wie viele Verkaufsstellen ein Produkt führen: intensiv (überall), selektiv (ausgewählte Partner), oder exklusiv (ein Partner pro Region).

segments.src: - **Omnichannel** — channels integrated to share inventory, pricing, and customer data so the experience feels like one brand, versus multichannel silos.
segments.tr: - **Omnichannel** — Kanäle, die integriert sind um Bestände, Preise und Kundendaten zu teilen, sodass die Erfahrung sich wie eine Marke anfühlt, im Gegensatz zu isolierten Multichannel-Silos.

segments.src: - **Channel conflict** — friction that arises when a new or existing channel undercuts another, e.g., a brand's direct site competing with its own retail partners.
segments.tr: - **Kanalkonflikt** — Reibung, die entsteht, wenn ein neuer oder vorhandener Kanal einen anderen unterwandert, z.B. wenn die direkte Website einer Marke mit ihren eigenen Handelspartnern konkurriert.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — C.** Maximum coverage for a low-consideration convenience good; shoppers won't search, so absence equals a lost sale.
segments.tr: *Antworten: **Frage 1 — C.** Maximale Abdeckung für ein niedriges Involvement Produkt; Käufer werden nicht suchen, daher keine Verfügbarkeit = verlorener Verkauf.

segments.src: **Q2 — X (False).** That's multichannel.
segments.tr: **Frage 2 — F (Falsch).** Das ist nur Multichannel.

segments.src: It only becomes omnichannel when the channels share inventory, pricing, and customer history — app stock visibility, in-store returns for online orders, and so on.
segments.tr: Es wird nur Omnichannel, wenn die Kanäle Bestände, Preise und Kundenhistorie teilen — Real-Time Bestandssichtbarkeit in der App, In-Store Rückgaben für Online-Bestellungen usw.

segments.src: **Q3 — B.** Channel functions can be shifted, not eliminated; whoever drops out hands the warehousing, shipping, credit, and returns work to someone else — usually the brand.
segments.tr: **Frage 3 — B.** Vertriebsfunktionen können verschoben, aber nicht eliminiert werden; wer den Weg beschreitet, übergibt die Lagerhaltung, den Versand, die Kreditvergabe und die Rückgabenbearbeitung an jemand anderen — normalerweise die Marke selbst.

segments.src: Prices don't automatically drop (A and C are the classic misconception), and going direct typically *increases* conflict risk rather than removing it (D).*
segments.tr: Preise fallen nicht automatisch (A und C sind das klassische Missverständnis), und zur Direktverteilung überzugehen erhöht normalerweise das Konfliktrisiko statt es zu verringern (D).*

vi.title: [Marketing 101 #9] Sản phẩm tốt nhất không phải là người chiến thắng. Cái bạn thực sự có thể có được mới là.

segments.src: > "Place" isn't about where a product sits. It's about how many steps stand between wanting it and holding it — and who does the work of removing them.
segments.tr: > "Địa điểm" không phải là về nơi một sản phẩm nằm. Nó là về có bao nhiêu bước nằm giữa việc muốn nó và nắm giữ nó — và ai làm công việc loại bỏ chúng.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Khái niệm hôm nay

segments.src: Of marketing's four Ps — product, price, promotion, place — **place** is the least glamorous and quietly the most decisive.
segments.tr: Trong bốn P của marketing — product, price, promotion, place — **place** là ít quyến rũ nhất và một cách im lặng là quyết định nhất.

segments.src: It's shorthand for *distribution*: the path a product travels from whoever made it to whoever uses it.
segments.tr: Đó là cách viết tắt cho *distribution*: đường dẫn một sản phẩm đi từ người làm nó đến người sử dụng nó.

segments.src: Two questions define that path.
segments.tr: Hai câu hỏi xác định đường dẫn đó.

segments.src: How many hops?**
segments.tr: Bao nhiêu bước?**

segments.src: A **direct channel** goes maker → customer: a farmers market stand, a brand's own website, a factory outlet.
segments.tr: Một **direct channel** đi từ nhà sản xuất → khách hàng: một quầy hàng chợ nông sản, trang web của chính thương hiệu, cửa hàng bán lẻ nhà máy.

segments.src: An **indirect channel** adds **intermediaries**: manufacturer → wholesaler/distributor → retailer → you.
segments.tr: Một **indirect channel** thêm **intermediaries**: nhà sản xuất → nhà bán buôn/nhà phân phối → nhà bán lẻ → bạn.

segments.src: Each hop takes a slice of margin.
segments.tr: Mỗi bước lấy một phần lợi nhuận.

segments.src: Each hop also does real work.
segments.tr: Mỗi bước cũng làm công việc thực sự.

segments.src: That's the part people get wrong.
segments.tr: Đó là phần mọi người hiểu sai.

segments.src: The common complaint is that middlemen are markup for nothing.
segments.tr: Thàn phàn chung là những người trung gian là chi phí không có gì.

segments.src: But distribution functions can be *shifted*, not *eliminated*.
segments.tr: Nhưng các chức năng phân phối có thể *chuyển dịch*, không phải *loại bỏ*.

segments.src: Somebody has to:
segments.tr: Ai đó phải:

segments.src: - **Break bulk** — turn a truckload into a shelf's worth
segments.tr: - **Break bulk** — biến một chuyến xe tải thành giá trị một kệ

segments.src: - **Carry inventory** and absorb the risk that it doesn't sell
segments.tr: - **Carry inventory** và hấp thụ rủi ro nó không bán được

segments.src: - **Extend credit** so a small store can stock before it sells
segments.tr: - **Extend credit** để một cửa hàng nhỏ có thể tích trữ trước khi bán

segments.src: - **Assemble assortment** so you don't visit 40 brand websites for one shopping trip
segments.tr: - **Assemble assortment** để bạn không phải ghé thăm 40 trang web thương hiệu cho một chuyến mua sắm

segments.src: - **Handle returns**, damage, and customer questions
segments.tr: - **Handle returns**, thiệt hại và các câu hỏi của khách hàng

segments.src: Cut the distributor and you inherit the warehouse, the trucks, the credit risk, and the returns desk.
segments.tr: Cắt giảm nhà phân phối và bạn kế thừa nhà kho, những chiếc xe tải, rủi ro tín dụng và bàn làm việc hoàn trả.

segments.src: Sometimes that's worth it.
segments.tr: Đôi khi điều đó là đáng giá.

segments.src: It's never free.
segments.tr: Nó không bao giờ miễn phí.

segments.src: How widely?**
segments.tr: Rộng bao nhiêu?**

segments.src: This is **distribution intensity**, and it has three settings:
segments.tr: Đây là **distribution intensity**, và nó có ba cài đặt:

segments.src: - **Intensive** — everywhere physically possible. Soda, gum, phone chargers, sunscreen. Nobody drives across town for a Coke; if it isn't there, the sale goes to whatever *is*.
segments.tr: - **Intensive** — ở mọi nơi có thể. Nước soda, kẹo cao su, sạc điện thoại, kem chống nắng. Không ai lái xe xuyên thành phố để lấy một Coke; nếu nó không ở đó, bán hàng sẽ đi đến bất cứ cái nào *có*.

segments.src: - **Selective** — a curated set of partners. Appliances, mid-tier cosmetics, running shoes. Enough coverage to be findable, few enough to keep service quality up.
segments.tr: - **Selective** — một tập hợp được lựa chọn của các đối tác. Các thiết bị, mỹ phẩm tầm trung, giày chạy. Đủ phủ sóng để tìm được, ít đủ để giữ chất lượng dịch vụ.

segments.src: - **Exclusive** — one partner per territory. Luxury watches, car dealerships, high-end audio. Scarcity and service are part of the product.
segments.tr: - **Exclusive** — một đối tác trên mỗi lãnh thổ. Đồng hồ xa xỉ, đại lý ô tô, âm thanh cao cấp. Sự khan hiếm và dịch vụ là một phần của sản phẩm.

segments.src: The right setting follows how people shop.
segments.tr: Cài đặt đúng theo cách mọi người mua sắm.

segments.src: The less someone is willing to search, the more intensive you must be.
segments.tr: Càng ít ai sẵn sàng tìm kiếm, bạn phải càng rộng rãi.

segments.src: **Multichannel vs.
segments.tr: **Multichannel so với

segments.src: omnichannel.** These get used interchangeably and shouldn't be.
segments.tr: omnichannel.** Những cái này được sử dụng thay thế cho nhau và không nên như vậy.

segments.src: *Multichannel* means you sell in several places, each running as its own silo — the website has no idea what the store has.
segments.tr: *Multichannel* có nghĩa là bạn bán ở nhiều nơi, mỗi nơi chạy như một silo riêng — trang web không biết cửa hàng có cái gì.

segments.src: *Omnichannel* means those channels share inventory, pricing, and customer history, so the shopper experiences one brand instead of three departments.
segments.tr: *Omnichannel* có nghĩa là những kênh đó chia sẻ hàng tồn kho, giá cả và lịch sử khách hàng, vì vậy người mua sắm trải nghiệm một thương hiệu thay vì ba bộ phận.

segments.src: Buy online / pick up in store, return an online order at the register, ship-from-store, an app that shows real stock at the location nearest you — those are omnichannel plumbing, not marketing copy.
segments.tr: Mua trực tuyến / lấy tại cửa hàng, hoàn trả đơn hàng trực tuyến tại quầy, giao từ cửa hàng, một ứng dụng hiển thị hàng tồn kho thực tại vị trí gần nhất với bạn — đó là đường ống toàn kênh, không phải bản sao tiếp thị.

segments.src: **Channel conflict** is the standard failure mode: a new channel eats an existing one.
segments.tr: **Channel conflict** là chế độ lỗi tiêu chuẩn: một kênh mới ăn cái hiện có.

segments.src: A brand launches a direct site priced below the retailers who built its shelf presence, and those retailers quietly cut their orders.
segments.tr: Một thương hiệu ra mắt một trang web trực tiếp với giá thấp hơn các nhà bán lẻ đã xây dựng sự hiện diện trên kệ của nó, và những nhà bán lẻ đó im lặng cắt giảm đơn hàng của họ.

segments.src: Companies manage this with consistent pricing, channel-specific assortments (the exclusive colorway only Dick's gets), and minimum advertised price policies.
segments.tr: Các công ty quản lý điều này bằng giá cả nhất quán, phân loại cụ thể theo kênh (màu sắc độc quyền chỉ Dick's nhận được) và chính sách giá quảng cáo tối thiểu.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Trong cuộc sống hàng ngày

segments.src: It's Thursday night in Dallas.
segments.tr: Đó là tối thứ năm ở Dallas.

segments.src: Your kid's birthday party is Saturday and the one thing they asked for is a specific LEGO set.
segments.tr: Bữa tiệc sinh nhật của con bạn là Thứ Bảy và thứ duy nhất họ yêu cầu là một bộ LEGO cụ thể.

segments.src: You have options, and each is a different channel structure.
segments.tr: Bạn có các tùy chọn, và mỗi cái là một cấu trúc kênh khác nhau.

segments.src: LEGO's own site is **direct**.
segments.tr: Trang web của chính LEGO là **direct**.

segments.src: Amazon is a retailer plus a marketplace of third-party sellers.
segments.tr: Amazon là một nhà bán lẻ cộng với một thị trường của những người bán bên thứ ba.

segments.src: Target and Walmart are **retailers** buying at wholesale.
segments.tr: Target và Walmart là **retailers** mua buôn.

segments.src: The independent toy shop two miles away buys through a **distributor**.
segments.tr: Cửa hàng đồ chơi độc lập hai dặm xa mua qua một **distributor**.

segments.src: You open the Target app, see that the store off I-35 has one on the shelf, order it, and pick it up in an hour.
segments.tr: Bạn mở ứng dụng Target, thấy cửa hàng ngoài I-35 có một cái trên kệ, đặt hàng nó và nhận nó trong một giờ.

segments.src: Trace what had to happen for that hour to exist.
segments.tr: Theo dõi những gì phải xảy ra để giờ đó tồn tại.

segments.src: The set was molded in a factory, containerized, shipped across an ocean, cleared customs, sat in a regional distribution center, rode a truck to that store, got scanned onto a shelf — and the app knew, at store level, that it was there.
segments.tr: Bộ này được đúc trong một nhà máy, đóng container, vận chuyển qua đại dương, đã qua hải quan, nằm trong một trung tâm phân phối khu vực, được chở trên một chiếc xe tải đến cửa hàng đó, được quét lên một kệ — và ứng dụng biết, ở cấp cửa hàng, rằng nó ở đó.

segments.src: That last part is the omnichannel piece.
segments.tr: Phần cuối cùng là phần toàn kênh.

segments.src: Same price in the aisle and in the app; an employee picks it; and if it's the wrong set, you can return it at the counter even though you "bought it online."
segments.tr: Cùng giá trong lối đi và trong ứng dụng; một nhân viên chọn nó; và nếu nó là bộ sai, bạn có thể hoàn trả nó tại quầy mặc dù bạn "mua nó trực tuyến."

segments.src: The little toy shop has it too, at full price.
segments.tr: Cửa hàng đồ chơi nhỏ cũng có nó, với giá đầy đủ.

segments.src: It can stock a few thousand different items without opening a few thousand supplier accounts, because a distributor bought the pallet and sold it a case of six.
segments.tr: Nó có thể tích trữ một vài nghìn mục khác nhau mà không mở vài nghìn tài khoản nhà cung cấp, vì một nhà phân phối đã mua pallet và bán nó một trường hợp sáu.

segments.src: That's breaking bulk, and it's the entire reason small retail can exist.
segments.tr: Đó là chia tách số lượng, và đó là lý do duy nhất bán lẻ nhỏ có thể tồn tại.

segments.src: Direct looks like a landslide — until you ask how many people were going to type your URL on a Thursday night.
segments.tr: Direct trông giống như một lở đất — cho đến khi bạn hỏi có bao nhiêu người sẽ gõ URL của bạn vào tối thứ năm.

segments.src: Retail costs more than half the margin and delivers something direct can't manufacture: being already there, in the store the customer was going to anyway.
segments.tr: Bán lẻ chi phí hơn một nửa lợi nhuận và cung cấp một cái gì đó trực tiếp không thể sản xuất: đã ở đó, trong cửa hàng mà khách hàng sẽ đi.

segments.src: Most brands run both, and spend a lot of effort keeping them from cannibalizing each other.
segments.tr: Hầu hết các thương hiệu chạy cả hai, và dành nhiều nỗ lực để giữ họ không ăn thịt lẫn nhau.

segments.src: That's the whole discipline in one sentence: **place is the practice of buying availability, and deciding what it's worth.**
segments.tr: Đó là toàn bộ kỷ luật trong một câu: **place (địa điểm) là thực hành mua tính sẵn có và quyết định nó đáng giá bao nhiêu.**

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Tóm tắt 3 dòng

segments.src: 1. Place = distribution: the route from maker to user, defined by how many intermediaries are in it and how widely the product is stocked.
segments.tr: 1. Place = distribution: tuyến đường từ người làm đến người dùng, được xác định bởi bao nhiêu trung gian ở trong đó và sản phẩm được tích trữ rộng rãi như thế nào.

segments.src: 2. Intermediaries aren't optional overhead — they perform functions (breaking bulk, inventory risk, credit, assortment, returns) that someone has to perform, so removing them means absorbing them.
segments.tr: 2. Trung gian không phải là chi phí chọn lựa — họ thực hiện các chức năng (chia tách số lượng, rủi ro hàng tồn kho, tín dụng, phân loại, hoàn trả) mà ai đó phải thực hiện, vì vậy loại bỏ họ có nghĩa là hấp thụ họ.

segments.src: 3. Omnichannel isn't "selling in many places"; it's channels sharing inventory, price, and customer data so the shopper meets one brand — and adding channels always risks conflict with the ones you already have.
segments.tr: 3. Omnichannel (toàn kênh) không phải là "bán ở nhiều nơi"; nó là các kênh chia sẻ hàng tồn kho, giá và dữ liệu khách hàng để người mua sắm gặp một thương hiệu — và thêm các kênh luôn có rủi ro xung đột với những cái bạn đã có.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Câu hỏi tự kiểm tra

segments.src: **Q1.** A beverage company wants its new sports drink in every gas station, vending machine, and grocery store it can reach.
segments.tr: **Q1.** Một công ty thức uống muốn nước uống thể thao mới của nó ở mọi trạm xăng, máy bán hàng tự động và cửa hàng tạp hóa mà nó có thể tìm được.

segments.src: Which distribution intensity is this?
segments.tr: Cường độ phân phối này là gì?

segments.src: A) Exclusive B) Selective C) Intensive D) Direct-only
segments.tr: A) Exclusive B) Selective C) Intensive D) Direct-only

segments.src: **Q2.** (O/X) A company that sells through its website, a mobile app, and physical stores is by definition running an omnichannel strategy.
segments.tr: **Q2.** (O/X) Một công ty bán qua trang web, ứng dụng di động và các cửa hàng vật lý của nó theo định nghĩa đang chạy chiến lược toàn kênh.

segments.src: **Q3.** A furniture brand shuts down its wholesale distributor to "cut out the middleman."
segments.tr: **Q3.** Một thương hiệu nội thất tắt nhà phân phối bán buôn của nó để "cắt giảm người trung gian."

segments.src: Which is the most likely consequence?
segments.tr: Hệ quả nào là có khả năng nhất?

segments.src: A) The distribution functions disappear along with the distributor
segments.tr: A) Các chức năng phân phối biến mất cùng với nhà phân phối

segments.src: B) The brand must now carry inventory, ship to stores, and manage returns itself
segments.tr: B) Thương hiệu bây giờ phải mang hàng tồn kho, vận chuyển đến các cửa hàng và quản lý hoàn trả chính nó

segments.src: C) Retail prices automatically fall by the distributor's full margin
segments.tr: C) Giá bán lẻ tự động giảm xuống toàn bộ lợi nhuận của nhà phân phối

segments.src: D) Channel conflict becomes impossible
segments.tr: D) Xung đột kênh trở nên bất khả thi

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Các thuật ngữ hôm nay

segments.src: - **Distribution channel** — the set of organizations that move a product from producer to end user.
segments.tr: - **Distribution channel** — tập hợp các tổ chức chuyển sản phẩm từ nhà sản xuất đến người dùng cuối.

segments.src: - **Intermediary** — a wholesaler, distributor, or retailer that performs channel functions such as breaking bulk, holding inventory, and extending credit.
segments.tr: - **Intermediary** — một nhà bán buôn, nhà phân phối hoặc nhà bán lẻ thực hiện các chức năng kênh như chia tách số lượng, giữ hàng tồn kho và cấp tín dụng.

segments.src: - **Distribution intensity** — how many outlets carry the product: intensive (everywhere), selective (a curated set), or exclusive (one per territory).
segments.tr: - **Distribution intensity** — bao nhiêu cửa hàng bán sản phẩm: intensive (mọi nơi), selective (một tập hợp được lựa chọn) hoặc exclusive (một trên mỗi lãnh thổ).

segments.src: - **Omnichannel** — channels integrated to share inventory, pricing, and customer data so the experience feels like one brand, versus multichannel silos.
segments.tr: - **Omnichannel** — các kênh được tích hợp để chia sẻ hàng tồn kho, giá và dữ liệu khách hàng để trải nghiệm cảm thấy như một thương hiệu, so với các silo đa kênh.

segments.src: - **Channel conflict** — friction that arises when a new or existing channel undercuts another, e.g., a brand's direct site competing with its own retail partners.
segments.tr: - **Channel conflict** — ma sát phát sinh khi một kênh mới hoặc hiện có cắt giá kênh khác, ví dụ như trang web trực tiếp của thương hiệu cạnh tranh với các đối tác bán lẻ của nó.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — C.** Maximum coverage for a low-consideration convenience good; shoppers won't search, so absence equals a lost sale.
segments.tr: *Câu trả lời: **Q1 — C.** Phủ sóng tối đa cho hàng tiện lợi cân nhắc thấp; những người mua sắm sẽ không tìm kiếm, vì vậy sự vắng mặt bằng một bán hàng mất mát.

segments.src: **Q2 — X (False).** That's multichannel.
segments.tr: **Q2 — X (False).** Đó là multichannel.

segments.src: It only becomes omnichannel when the channels share inventory, pricing, and customer history — app stock visibility, in-store returns for online orders, and so on.
segments.tr: Nó chỉ trở thành omnichannel khi các kênh chia sẻ hàng tồn kho, giá cả và lịch sử khách hàng — khả năng hiển thị hàng tồn kho ứng dụng, hoàn trả tại cửa hàng cho các đơn hàng trực tuyến, v.v.

segments.src: **Q3 — B.** Channel functions can be shifted, not eliminated; whoever drops out hands the warehousing, shipping, credit, and returns work to someone else — usually the brand.
segments.tr: **Q3 — B.** Các chức năng kênh có thể được chuyển dịch, không phải bị loại bỏ; ai bỏ ra sẽ đưa công việc kho hàng, vận chuyển, tín dụng và hoàn trả cho người khác — thường là thương hiệu.

segments.src: Prices don't automatically drop (A and C are the classic misconception), and going direct typically *increases* conflict risk rather than removing it (D).*
segments.tr: Giá không giảm tự động (A và C là sự hiểu lầm cổ điển), và đi trực tiếp thường *tăng* rủi ro xung đột thay vì loại bỏ nó (D).*
